reviewStandard: All six routes fail the pre-generation structure, analyte-class, stereochemical-identity, molecular-complexity, canonical-synonym, or ecological-composition gate. They receive no marked prompt, generation call, or raster.
promotionRule: No Batch 095 route is eligible for generation or promotion until its exact enzyme/species/assembly, toxin/analyte panel, stereochemical depiction source, vancomycin representation, canonical route identity, or niche-specific virome composition is corrected and independently re-audited.

routeDecisions.reason: The route spans ureases from multiple prokaryotic and eukaryotic species, catalytic and apo states, distinct accessory systems, active-site metalation, and organism-specific oligomeric assemblies without selecting one sequence, species, assembly, structure accession, or biochemical state.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Choose one species and exact urease subunit or complex, sequence/accession, oligomeric and metalation state, ligand/substrate state, structure accession or explicitly non-structural reaction boundary, compartment, and claim scope.

routeDecisions.reason: The controlled term is a class of retained biological solutes, while the route combines indoxyl sulfate, p-cresyl sulfate, trimethylamine N-oxide, protein binding, microbial production, renal clearance, and several host effects as one visual subject.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Split by exact analyte and chemical form, precursor, organism/pathway, specimen, protein-bound fraction, concentration and units, renal-function stratum, assay, comparator, endpoint, and evidence tier.

routeDecisions.reason: UDCA is an exact C24 steroid whose identity depends on multiple stereocenters, including the 7-beta hydroxyl orientation that distinguishes it from related bile acids. A generated heavy-atom connectivity model would not independently verify those stereochemical assignments and could falsely depict a related bile acid as UDCA.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Use an independently licensed or project-rendered structure derived deterministically from the authoritative CID/ChEBI connection table with explicit stereochemical validation, then audit atom count, bond graph, stereocenters, protonation state, conformation boundary, and derivative framing.

routeDecisions.reason: Vancomycin is a 1449.2-Da glycopeptide with 66 carbons, 24 oxygens, 9 nitrogens, 2 chlorines, many stereocenters, and no PubChem computed 3D conformer because the record exceeds its conformer limits. A one-call generated molecular portrait cannot be literally verified at this complexity, while a generic vial or powder would not establish chemical identity.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Approve a deterministic structure rendering from an authoritative connection table or an exact labeled product/specimen record, including form and salt, stereochemistry, protonation, hydration, formulation, structure source, license, and non-photographic boundary.

routeDecisions.reason: NLM MeSH treats Viral Microbiome as an entry term for Virome, and the local page states that it is a redirect and cross-reference to the comprehensive virome page while still occupying a separate canonical route. A separate image would duplicate or contradict one controlled concept.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Retire this route to a permanent alias of virome, or define a narrower non-duplicative niche, specimen, viral fraction, sequencing method, taxonomic scope, population, and evidence boundary before media review.

routeDecisions.reason: MeSH defines a virome as all viruses within a particular biological niche. The route combines bacteriophages, eukaryotic viruses, endogenous elements, many host sites and diseases, ecological interactions, sequencing observations, and therapy; no exact niche, specimen, composition, taxonomy, or measured community is selected.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Define one biological niche and specimen, collection and viral-enrichment protocol, sequencing platform and database version, taxonomic or vOTU composition, abundance threshold, host assignment method, population/model, comparator, time point, and whether the image represents measured data or a reviewed orientation atlas.
